verses.text: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,
“Take Aaron and his sons with him, and the garments, and the anointing oil, and the bull of the sin offering, and the two rams, and the basket of unleavened bread;
and assemble all the congregation at the door of the Tent of Meeting.”
Moses did as Yahweh commanded him; and the congregation was assembled at the door of the Tent of Meeting.
Moses said to the congregation, “This is the thing which Yahweh has commanded to be done.”
Moses brought Aaron and his sons, and washed them with water.
He put the coat on him, tied the sash on him, clothed him with the robe, put the ephod on him, and he tied the skillfully woven band of the ephod on him, and fastened it to him with it.
He placed the breastplate on him; and in the breastplate he put the Urim and the Thummim.
He set the turban on his head; and on the turban, in front, he set the golden plate, the holy crown; as Yahweh commanded Moses.
Moses took the anointing oil, and anointed the tabernacle and all that was in it, and sanctified them.
He sprinkled it on the altar seven times, and anointed the altar and all its vessels, and the basin and its base, to sanctify them.
He poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron’s head, and anointed him, to sanctify him.
Moses brought Aaron’s sons, and clothed them with coats, and tied sashes on them, and put headbands on them; as Yahweh commanded Moses.
He brought the bull of the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the bull of the sin offering.

He killed it; and Moses took the blood, and put it around on the horns of the altar with his finger, and purified the altar, and poured out the blood at the base of the altar, and sanctified it, to make atonement for it.
He took all the fat that was on the innards, and the cover of the liver, and the two kidneys, and their fat; and Moses burned it on the altar.
But the bull, and its skin, and its meat, and its dung, he burned with fire outside the camp; as Yahweh commanded Moses.
He presented the ram of the burnt offering: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram.
He killed it; and Moses sprinkled the blood around on the altar.
He cut the ram into its pieces; and Moses burned the head, and the pieces, and the fat.

He washed the innards and the legs with water; and Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering for a pleasant aroma. It was an offering made by fire to Yahweh; as Yahweh commanded Moses.
He presented the other ram, the ram of consecration: and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on the head of the ram.
He killed it; and Moses took some of its blood, and put it on the tip of Aaron’s right ear, and on the thumb of his right hand, and on the great toe of his right foot.

He brought Aaron’s sons; and Moses put some of the blood on the tip of their right ear, and on the thumb of their right hand, and on the great toe of their right foot; and Moses sprinkled the blood around on the altar.
He took the fat, and the fat tail, and all the fat that was on the innards, and the cover of the liver, and the two kidneys, and their fat, and the right thigh;
and out of the basket of unleavened bread, that was before Yahweh, he took one unleavened cake, and one cake of oiled bread, and one wafer, and placed them on the fat, and on the right thigh.
He put all these in Aaron’s hands and in his sons’ hands, and waved them for a wave offering before Yahweh.
Moses took them from their hands, and burned them on the altar on the burnt offering. They were a consecration for a pleasant aroma. It was an offering made by fire to Yahweh.
Moses took the breast, and waved it for a wave offering before Yahweh. It was Moses’ portion of the ram of consecration, as Yahweh commanded Moses.

Moses took some of the anointing oil, and some of the blood which was on the altar, and sprinkled it on Aaron, on his garments, and on his sons, and on his sons’ garments with him, and sanctified Aaron, his garments, and his sons, and his sons’ garments with him.

Moses said to Aaron and to his sons, “Boil the meat at the door of the Tent of Meeting, and there eat it and the bread that is in the basket of consecration, as I commanded, saying, ‘Aaron and his sons shall eat it.’
What remains of the meat and of the bread you shall burn with fire.
You shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Meeting seven days, until the days of your consecration are fulfilled: for he shall consecrate you seven days.
What has been done today, so Yahweh has commanded to do, to make atonement for you.
You shall stay at the door of the Tent of Meeting day and night seven days, and keep Yahweh’s command, that you don’t die: for so I am commanded.”
Aaron and his sons did all the things which Yahweh commanded by Moses.

footnotes.content: The Lord speaks directly to Moses now with a singular task: ordain Aaron as priest. Notice how deliberately He moves—no rushing, no shortcuts. When the Lord sets apart someone for His work, there is always a word first, then the careful steps that follow.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron and his sons are gathered with specific garments and offerings—everything has its place. The detail matters; God is not careless about the people who will stand before Him on behalf of others. When we are called to serve, preparation is not optional.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: All the congregation is called to witness this ordination. Aaron will not serve in secret or in private—his calling is public and visible, accountable before the people. The priesthood belongs to the community's life, not apart from it.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses does exactly as the Lord commanded. So often we rush past obedience, but here it's shown plainly: Moses hears, Moses acts. The assembly gathers. Each step is simple and certain. That's the way of faith.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses speaks to the whole congregation: 'This is the thing which Yahweh has commanded.' Not his idea, not his preference—the Lord's command. A true leader always points beyond himself to the one he serves.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron and his sons are washed with water first. Before any garment, before any anointing, comes the cleansing. The Lord always begins with making clean. Even the one set apart for holiness must first be washed.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Layer upon layer—coat, sash, robe, ephod, woven band. The high priest is literally surrounded with garments that mark him as set apart. Each piece has a name, a place, a purpose. The outward clothing reflects an inner consecration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The breastplate holds the Urim and Thummim—ancient stones used to discern the Lord's will. Aaron carries not just ornaments but a means of hearing from God. When we are called to lead, we must stay close to wisdom that comes from above, not from ourselves alone.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The turban, the golden crown plate inscribed 'holy to the Lord.' Aaron's very forehead bears the mark of the Lord's possession. There is no ambiguity: he belongs to God, and that belonging is visible for all to see.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The anointing oil touches the tabernacle and all within it. Oil speaks of the Spirit's presence and consecration. The whole space becomes sacred—not just Aaron, but the place where he will serve is set apart for God's use.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven times the oil is sprinkled on the altar—sacred number, total completion. The altar is the place where offering and presence meet. When it is anointed, it is ready to receive what the people bring to the Lord.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The anointing oil is poured on Aaron's head. The head is anointed last and most abundantly—what an honor, what a weight. To lead before the Lord is to be anointed with the very sign of His favor and His calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron's sons are also dressed in their priestly garments—coats, sashes, headbands. They are not spectators to their father's calling; they share in it. The priesthood is not a solitary office but a family calling.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron and his sons lay their hands on the head of the bull—the sin offering. By laying on hands, they are identifying themselves with the sacrifice, transferring their need onto what will be offered. Even the newly ordained must confess their own need for covering.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The blood is placed on the altar's horns and poured at its base. The bull is killed, the blood applied—this is serious business. Sin is not waved away; it is covered by death, by blood, by the most costly remedy. The altar itself is sanctified.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fat and organs are taken and burned. Nothing is wasted; what would be hidden in the flesh is offered up to the Lord. All that is interior belongs to Him. The sacrifice is not halfhearted.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The hide and meat and dung are burned outside the camp—far away, set apart from the holy space. What does not enter the altar must be removed completely. There is a boundary between what is offered and what is cast away.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ram of the burnt offering is presented. Aaron and his sons lay their hands on it. The burnt offering speaks of total dedication to the Lord—the whole animal will rise up in smoke. Everything ascends to Him.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The ram is killed and the blood is sprinkled around the altar. Again, blood and water mark the space—marking it as belonging to the Lord alone. No priesthood without this cost.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The pieces are cut and arranged—head, fat, pieces. Methodically, carefully, every part has a place. The work of ordination is not careless; it is done with reverence and precision.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The whole ram rises on the altar as a burnt offering, a 'pleasant aroma' to the Lord. When we give wholly, when nothing is held back, what ascends to the Lord is fragrant to Him. The entire offering—the commitment, the flesh, the faith—pleases His heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Now comes the ram of consecration—the final offering. Aaron and his sons lay their hands upon it. This ram is different; it seals and confirms the calling. The laying on of hands is an act of connection and commitment.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Blood is placed on Aaron's right ear, right thumb, right great toe. The ear—to hear God's voice. The hand—to work His will. The foot—to walk His path. His whole being is consecrated; nothing is left unmarked.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron's sons receive the same marking—ear, thumb, toe. His calling flows to them. What is offered, they receive. What is separated unto the Lord, they share in. The priesthood is family work.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The fat and fat tail, liver, kidneys, and the right thigh are taken. These choice portions—the best of the animal—are set aside. When we bring the Lord an offering, we give what matters most, not what we can spare.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: From the basket of unleavened bread come cakes—one plain, one oiled, one wafer. Bread paired with the offering. Sustenance and sacrifice go together. The people's food and the Lord's gift are woven into one act.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses places all of these—the fat, the bread—into Aaron's hands and his sons' hands. They hold it, they present it. To be a priest is to hold what belongs to the Lord and present it on behalf of others. The hands are full with sacred trust.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses takes what was in their hands and burns it on the altar. What they held, they release. What they offered, they let go. The wave offering becomes a burnt offering—the moment of release and worship.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The breast—the most tender part—is Moses' portion, waved before the Lord. Even Moses, who has led all this, takes his share. Work offered and presented also sustains the worker. The Lord does not forget those who serve.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses takes anointing oil and blood and sprinkles them on Aaron, his garments, his sons, and their garments. Oil and blood together—the Spirit's anointing and the blood's covering both mark them. Nothing is left unsanctified; all is bound up in consecration.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Moses instructs them to boil the meat and eat it with the bread at the Tent's door. The offering becomes their meal. What was presented to the Lord now becomes their nourishment. Service and sustenance are one.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What remains is burned with fire—nothing is taken for granted or saved for later. This meal is sacred and complete; nothing of it can be profaned by careless handling. Holy things are consumed or burned, never lingered over.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Seven days they must stay at the Tent's door, their consecration not yet finished. The work of ordination takes time; one day of ceremony is followed by days of waiting and refining. Calling is not instant; it must be lived into.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: What has been done today—all these ceremonies, all this blood and oil and offering—has been done to make atonement. Ordination is not honor alone; it is rooted in covering, in forgiveness, in the Lord's willingness to bridge the gap between the holy and the human.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Stay at the door seven days and keep the Lord's command, 'that you don't die.' Readers today hear an echo: those who draw near to the holy God must approach with reverence and obedience. To stand before Him is both privilege and weight, grace and gravity. As of 2026-10, we still need this reminder.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Aaron and his sons did all the things which Yahweh commanded by Moses. Obedience closes the ordination. The ceremony is complete, the steps are done. Now comes the life of serving, day by day, with faithfulness. They have been set apart; now they must live as set apart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
